=== REPORT ===
"The observable process which Schiller and Dewey particularly singled out for generalization is the familiar one by which any individual settles into NEW OPINIONS." [dangling: "Schiller and Dewey"]. Kept. These are proper names, so they identify their referents and are not referring words that need an antecedent.

"The process here is always the same." [dangling: "The process"]. Kept. The previous statement in the note supplies the process, and that statement does not dangle.

"Failure to take account of the part played by the older truths is the source of much of the unjust criticism leveled against pragmatism." [dangling: "the older truths"]. Kept. Earlier statements in the note supply this referent: "It preserves the older stock of truths…", and the individual's "stock of old opinions" in paragraph 1. The dropped "The point I now urge you to observe" is only stance.

"Their influence is absolutely controlling." [dangling: "Their"]. Kept. The previous statement names the older truths, so "Their" resolves. That statement is a contiguous stitch of adjacent spans and does not dangle.

"Loyalty to them is the first principle…" [dangling: "them"]. Kept. It resolves to the older truths in the same way as the statement above.

"A new opinion counts as 'true' just in proportion…" [dangling]. Kept. The check itself passes it.

"It must both lean on old truth and grasp new fact; and its success in doing this, is a matter for the individual's appreciation." [cut lost content]. Kept. "(as I said a moment ago)" is only a pointer, so the cut is allowed. "its" resolves to the new opinion in the previous statement.

"Now Dewey and Schiller proceed to generalize this observation and to apply it to the most ancient parts of truth." [dangling: "this observation"]. Kept. The previous paragraph of the note gives the observation: how new truth grows by grafting onto old.

"They also once were plastic.", "They also were called true for human reasons." and "They also mediated…". Kept. "They" resolves to "the most ancient parts of truth" in the statement before them.

"Mr. Schiller still gives to all this view of truth the name of 'Humanism,' but, for this doctrine too, the name of pragmatism seems fairly to be in the ascendant." [dangling: "all this view of truth"]. Kept. The view of truth set out across the note's preceding paragraphs is the antecedent.

"Such then would be the scope of pragmatism…" [dangling]. Kept. The check passes it.

"Failure to take account of… is the source of much of the unjust criticism…" [weak]. Kept. The check passes it on support, and the spans are contiguous.

"The trail of the human serpent is thus over everything." [dangling: "thus"]. Kept. "thus" points back to the statements just before it, which are in the note.

"The trail of the human serpent is thus over everything." [reads-alone dangling: "the human serpent"]. Kept. This is a metaphor in the author's own words, not a reference to an earlier antecedent. Its sense, that human reasons shape all truth, comes from the preceding statements in the note.

"It preserves the older stock of truths…", "The reasons why we call things true…" and "The ancient formulas are reinterpreted…" [dangling]. Kept. The check passes all three.

No edits were made.
